custody:sign:user: Demandable but deliberately unmintable. /v1/sign validates the claimed purpose against PURPOSES (src/server.ts:110, :429), which includes 'user', so the gate at src/server.ts:433 can demand custody:sign:user — but purposeGate (src/gates.ts:103) refuses user-purpose rows unconditionally: a user-purpose wallet exists so the customer can hold and export it, and the platform signs nothing on their behalf (SD-07). Registering the scope would let identity mint a capability this service exists to refuse.
custody:sign:pool: Demandable but deliberately unmintable, for the same reason as custody:sign:user above and by the same mechanism. Migration 8 widened the purpose CHECK to admit 'pool' (src/migrations.ts), so /v1/sign accepts it as a claimed purpose and the gate synthesises this scope name from the purpose set it closes over (src/server.ts) — but SIGNABLE_PURPOSES in src/gates.ts is {deployer, treasury, deposit}, 'pool' is not in it, and purposeGate refuses every pool-purpose row before a key is touched. The absence is the design, not an omission: a mining pool's payout key holds coin that is owed to the miners who found the block, and the destinations it would pay to are chosen by PPLNS accounting inside micro-pool, which custody cannot see and has no basis to authorise. 36-multi-chain-and-mining-pool.md §5.3 pays miners by crediting the ledger rather than by moving that coin, so refusing strands nothing. Registering the scope would let identity mint authority to spend a pool's payout key — the one capability this purpose must never carry. (This entry cites files only.
